info.title: WaveScan Paint Appearance API
info.description:
WaveScan paint-appearance API (slice 1).

Monthly Overview returns one PASS / WARNING / FAIL (or ungraded) per
model, colour and orientation mean, using `status_of` and stored
`cf_standard` rows. That grain is not a product pass rate. D1 stays
open. `grading_available` on meta and preview stays false. A client
that averages preview points or computes a status locally is inventing
an answer this platform has not made.

**Facts are immutable.** Measurements are never updated or deleted (ADR 0005).
Corrections are new rows; retirement is recorded, never applied in place.

Errors always have the shape `{statusCode, error, message, correlationId}`.

post.summary: Correct a measurement by adding a row. Engineer role.
post.description:
One transaction: the new row, the supersession record, the audit event.

The original is **not** edited. It stays in `wavescan` with the values it
always had and leaves the active reads because the supersession trigger
sets its flag -- the application holds no `UPDATE` on that table and could
not do it any other way (ADR 0005, `01-DATA-MODEL.md` §5).

Identity is not patchable: `plant`, `model`, `checkzone`, `color`,
`tolerance_group`, `paintline`, `load_id`, `source_sheet` and `source_row`
are not fields of the body, so sending one is a 422. They are copied from
the original inside the INSERT.

post.summary: Retire a committed batch. Admin role. Never deletes it.
post.description:
One column on `load_batch`, plus the audit event, in one transaction.

The batch's measurements are untouched. They stop appearing in every
reporting read because the active-data predicate tests the batch's status
(`01-DATA-MODEL.md` §5), not because anything happened to them -- so the
`wavescan` row count for this `load_id` is the same afterwards, and the
response says how many rows that is.

No `measurement_supersession` row is written. Retiring a batch is not a
claim that each reading was replaced by a better one; that claim is what a
correction makes, one row at a time.

post.summary: Propose a column or zone mapping, or apply an identity alias. Engineer role.
post.description:
Record a COLUMN/ZONE proposal, or apply an identity alias.

A 201 here changes how no file is read **for COLUMN and ZONE**. Identity
aliases (`ALIAS_COLOR`, rostered `ALIAS_MODEL`) are applied in this
same Engineer request (spec A2): alias + audit, replay if the batch
allows. Leftover programs (J73 / CX743 / V363 / U704) are 422 onto
Ranger; they may bind onto that program's own catalogue. A committed
remainder still keeps the alias when replay is refused. The similarity
score is carried for a person to read, not acted on.

`ZONE` (T29) is one complete, owner-proved checkpoint set for one plant
and one `ref_model` catalogue. It may omit `load_id` when `payload.plant_code`
names the plant (FVL has no committable batch); COLUMN and ALIAS_MODEL
still require it. `ALIAS_COLOR` is identity only (S12): it may omit
`load_id` when `payload.plant_code` names the plant, so a committed
remainder can teach future files without replaying facts. `422` for an
incomplete or padded set, a zone that is not a position on that model,
a blank proof field, a colour name not in `ref_color`, a leftover
spelling taught onto a foreign catalogue, or a `load_id` at another plant.

**`ZONE` takes a second shape (T86).** A payload carrying `matches`
instead of `mappings` is a guided panel-match set: N pairs of one of
this file's panel spellings onto a live panel of that plant x model,
which a person chose on `GET /mappings/panel-match`, plus the block of
live panels the **owner** says the set supersedes. It carries no proof
hash because it proves nothing and mints nothing; `decided_by` and
`method` record who said which panel each name is. `load_id` is
required. Still Engineer -> Admin, still all-or-none. `422` for a
spelling or a target named twice, a target that is not live at this
plant x model or is not a position on the model's own catalogue, a
panel both matched onto and retired, or a batch at another plant or in
a state that cannot replay.

`501` for a kind the data model declares and nothing implements
(`ALIAS_PLANT`, `ALIAS_CHECKZONE`, `ALIAS_PAINTLINE`).

get.summary: The guided panel-match screen for one batch and model. Any authenticated role.
get.description:
What this file calls each panel, what the plant's live panels are, and
which of those each file name **looks like by name** (T86).

The plant is the batch's own `load_batch.plant_code`; it is not a
parameter, so a caller cannot ask for one plant's panels against another
plant's file.

Every `candidates` entry is scored on the panel NAME with its leading
number removed, and every entry carries that score so the screen can
show how strong the match is. `raw_position` and `point_no` are shown
and never read: `14ROOF` is not proposed onto `14LFBOXSD` (D-86-3). An
empty `candidates` is an answer -- nothing in this platform fills it
with the nearest number.

A `live_panels` entry with `mappable = false` cannot be the target of a
confirmed pair, and `not_mappable_reason` says why in plain words.

post.summary: Approve a proposal, write the mapping, replay the batch if any. Admin role.
post.description:
One transaction: decision, alias, audit, replay enqueue.

* `404` — no such proposal.
* `409` — already decided, or the alias already exists, or the batch is
  in a state that cannot be replayed. In all three nothing is applied.
* `422` — the proposal's payload does not describe an applicable mapping.
  T04's diagnostic `COLUMN` rows are header diffs for a person to read;
  approving one means proposing the actual mapping first.
* `501` — a kind nothing implements.

**ZONE (T29).** All 32 rows or none, in this transaction. A missing row
is inserted APPROVED with the named owner's proof; a row that already
maps the same label to the same zone is certified in place; a row that
maps it to a *different* zone, or carries a different proof, is `409`
and nothing in the set is written. `zone_code` is never updated. With no
`load_id`, `replay` is null and no plant is onboarded. Approving never
sets `fixture_verified`.

**ZONE, panel-match shape (T86).** All N pairs, plus the owner's
retirement, in this one transaction. A pair whose spelling already maps
to the same panel is left alone; one that maps to a *different* panel is
`409` and nothing in the set is written. Retiring sets `retired_at` and
`retired_reason` on the named `ref_plant_ws_point` rows -- nothing is
deleted, so old measurements stay readable while new uploads stop
matching onto them (D-86-2).

satisfying the commit gate while leaving the record that somebody read
the older proposal.

blank one is a 422 here and a CHECK violation behind it.

post.summary: Append numeric overrides for one vehicle set and revalidate. Admin.
post.description:
One transaction: override rows, synchronous revalidation, audit event.

Append-only (`app_rw` can only add and read `review_override` rows). The
sheet is re-derived from its stored bytes by the ingest service with the
current overrides applied, its projection is rewritten (reset and
insert, never an in-place edit of a projection cell), and its
`review_revision` moves -- so an acknowledgement of the old revision no
longer satisfies the commit gate. The status stays PENDING_REVIEW; no
worker job is queued. `stg_raw` and each point's `raw` still show what
the file said, and commit inserts the overridden values.

post.summary: Retire a Film point: off the walk, kept in History. Engineer.
post.description:
T109 (D-109-4). Retire means "stop using this point", never "forget
it". The point leaves the live walk and stops feeding the dashboard's
Horizontal and Vertical **for every month**; the readings cars already
have on it stay in History, marked retired; no car becomes incomplete
because of it, because completeness counts live points on both sides; and
a later upload that writes its label is asked about in the row (D-109-6).

The only write is `retired_at` + `retired_reason`, which is the only
UPDATE the application holds on this table (revision 0035, D-109-9), with
an `audit_event` beside it. RO17: works with or without the point rules,
never on the last live point; `restore` brings a point back.

post.summary: Publish an owner-verified template profile version for this plant. Admin role.
post.description:
The only application path that can make a layout commit-capable.

One transaction: the appended profile version, its column policy, and the
`audit_event` naming the owner who verified it. The write itself happens
inside `publish_template_profile` in PostgreSQL, because `app_rw` holds
no INSERT or UPDATE on `ref_template_profile` -- which is what keeps the
Admin mapping-approve route from ever becoming a second door to this one,
however that route is later edited (design M6, spec S20).

The body names a workbook **already stored for this plant**, by hash; it
does not accept Excel. What is certified is therefore always bytes this
platform can replay.

Publishing then replays, from their stored bytes, the batches of this
plant and contract that are REJECTED_TEMPLATE or PENDING_REVIEW, and
returns their ids in `replayed_load_ids`. Replay ends at PENDING_REVIEW
or REJECTED_TEMPLATE. Publishing commits nothing and supersedes nothing:
an Engineer still presses commit on rows a person has read.

AcknowledgementCreate.title: AcknowledgementCreate

Read these warnings and accept them, for exactly these rows.

`review_revision` is required and is not a formality: it is what makes

revision no longer matches and the request is refused with 409 rather
than recorded against rows nobody read.

balanced.title: Balanced
balanced.description: rows_in_file == loaded + duplicate + rejected + quarantine. A batch cannot be committed unless this is true (docs/02-PIPELINE.md section 6).

plant_code.title: Plant Code
plant_code.description: The plant this batch is filed under: the expected_plant the upload declared, set when the batch was created and never re-derived from the rows (T17). Null only on batches created before that field existed.

template_fingerprint.title: Template Fingerprint
template_fingerprint.description: The EXACT ordered-layout hash of this sheet's header row: ordered recognised fields with gaps, plus sorted unrecognised extras. Since T26 this is provenance, not the profile selection key -- when it moves between one month and the next but semantic_signature does not, somebody reordered the columns and the contract is unchanged.

domain.title: Domain
domain.description: Which measurement vocabulary read this sheet: WAVESCAN (CF) or, since T46, FILMTHICKNESS (PELT FilmBuild layers, facts in the filmthickness table). The two never share header aliases or model spellings.

semantic_signature.title: Semantic Signature
semantic_signature.description: Hash of the sorted set of recognised logical fields for this domain. With domain and plant_code, this selects the template profile (T26). A reordered workbook signs the same and parses.

sheet_class.title: Sheet Class
sheet_class.description: WAVESCAN, FILMTHICKNESS (T46), OUT_OF_SCOPE_SHEET or UNKNOWN_DATA_SHEET, decided from the header row and never from the tab's name. A FILMTHICKNESS sheet's held rows carry reason EXTRA_POINT, UNMAPPED_POINT or FILM_MODEL_UNRESOLVED. An out-of-scope sheet (Methods, Color Data) is preserved evidence of another domain, not a broken WaveScan template; an unknown data-like sheet blocks for classification.

unreviewed_headers.title: Unreviewed Headers
unreviewed_headers.description: Headers of this sheet that are neither a recognised logical field nor a column an owner approved ignoring. Non-empty means UNREVIEWED_HEADER blocks the commit until somebody decides; nothing is ever auto-ignored.

profile_id.title: Profile Id
profile_id.description: The template profile that parsed this batch: the active ref_template_profile row for (domain, plant_code, semantic_signature) (T26; T18 keyed on the ordered fingerprint). Null when no profile claims this contract, which is why such a batch is REJECTED_TEMPLATE.

fixture_verified.title: Fixture Verified
fixture_verified.description: True when a fixture has proved this layout commits correctly. False when there is no profile, or a profile exists but has not been proved -- such a batch can be parsed and reviewed but not committed. Approving a header mapping does not set this.

review_revision.title: Review Revision
review_revision.description: Hash of the persisted review projection for this batch. Commit re-derives it from the stored bytes and refuses if it disagrees, so what was reviewed is what gets written (T18).

reject_reasons.title: Reject Reasons
reject_reasons.description: Counts by reject_log.reject_reason for this batch.

review_rows.title: Review Rows
review_rows.description: Rows in the persisted review projection: one per source row, whatever its disposition (T18).

review_dispositions.title: Review Dispositions
review_dispositions.description: Projection rows by disposition: LOAD, DUPLICATE, REJECT, QUARANTINE, and (T26) AGGREGATE_ROW -- a report roll-up such as a [All] hierarchy row, preserved and disclosed as a count and never written to wavescan. Aggregates are outside the balance equation, exactly as a blank row already is.

commit_blockers.title: Commit Blockers
commit_blockers.description: Stable tokens naming why this batch cannot be committed right now: NOT_PENDING_REVIEW, UNBALANCED, UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE, UNVERIFIED_PROFILE, NO_REVIEW_PROJECTION, VEHICLE_IDENTITY_MISSING, and (T26) UNREVIEWED_HEADER, DUPLICATE_LOGICAL_FIELD, PAINTLINE_MISSING, OUT_OF_SCOPE_SHEET, UNKNOWN_DATA_SHEET, AGGREGATE_ONLY_SHEET. Empty if and only if committable is true.

committable.title: Committable

A panel decision somebody already made, offered again (D-89-9).

Present only when this exact question has an earlier answer that does
not already resolve it: the pair is still `PROPOSED`, or it was taught

FilmColorSequenceEntry.title: FilmColorSequenceEntry
FilmColorSequenceEntry.description:
One colour's slot in the response's Base-ladder sequence (T73).

One sequence per response, shared by every layer (E-coat, Primer, Base,
Clear), every model and both orientations, at every plant. Sorted
ascending by: Base H lo, Base H hi, Base V lo, Base V hi (each null after
any number), family_order (null last), color_name. Horizontal is primary;
Vertical only breaks ties, and the colour has one rank for both
orientations. A partial range sorts its missing end after any present
value. No Base rule for H sorts after every colour with one; no Base rule
at all sorts after every laddered colour, by family order then name. The
Base values are the current published rule (latest-wins); the month
never changes them.

active_data_source.description: The view these facts were read through: not a duplicate, not superseded (01-DATA-MODEL.md section 10). Review rows, held labels (extra points, unmapped locations) and abandoned batches are never facts, so they are absent by construction.

FilmPointGridOut.title: FilmPointGridOut
FilmPointGridOut.description:
The whole catalogue of the vehicle's model, one entry per gold point.

Its length is the catalogue's (94 for Ranger / Raptor, 93 RAPCAP, 58
SGL), not the number of rows a file happened to contain.

point_no.title: Point No
point_no.description: ref_plant_film_point.point_no: the plant's walk order, for display. Never identity (F10, D-53-02).

orientation.title: Orientation
orientation.description: Hor / Ver of this plant's gold point (ref_plant_film_point; T47 for FVL-shaped lists, D-53-06 Hood / Roof / Floor = H for FTM). Null where nobody has proved it (non-FTM RAPCAP, SGL). Never computed from src_location_text or a row number.

src_location_text.title: Src Location Text
src_location_text.description: The plant's own spelling of the label that loaded onto this slot (e.g. FTM '029LTFTDOOR' on gold '022LTFTDOOR'). Null when no active fact exists for the point.

load_id.title: Load Id
load_id.description: The load that measured this point, or null.

source_row.title: Source Row
source_row.description: Its row in that sheet, or null.

counted.title: Counted
counted.description: T99 (D-99-2): whether the latest film_point_setting row says this point counts towards the dashboard's Hor / Ver. A point that does not count still appears here with its readings -- a point hidden from History is a point nobody can put back. True where no setting exists (every plant but FTM).

is_complete_stop.title: Is Complete Stop
is_complete_stop.description: T99 (D-99-8): a walk that ends exactly here is a complete vehicle, not a short one (FTM RAPCAP 059RTFEND and DBL 064RAPILLAR are no-box trucks). False everywhere else.

is_extra.title: Is Extra
is_extra.description: T109 (D-109-3): this point is beyond the plant's standard list for the model (FTM's 095RBXFLOOR and 096-098TGATEIN on the two DBL lists, and every point added since). A tag beside the point, not a grade.

retired.title: Retired
retired.description: T109 (D-109-4): this point is off the plant's live walk, and it is in this grid because **this car has a reading on it**. The reading is kept and shown, it no longer feeds the dashboard for any month, and it does not make this car incomplete -- completeness counts live points on both sides. A retired point with no reading on the car is not listed at all.

FilmPointOut.title: FilmPointOut
FilmPointOut.description: One slot of this plant's gold list for the model, measured or not.

FilmPointRestoreCreate.title: FilmPointRestoreCreate
FilmPointRestoreCreate.description:
RO17 (D-RO17-9): put a retired point back on the live list.

Refused when a live point holds its number, or when its code or current
label now names another point of the list.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why this point is gone. Required: it is the thing a reader of the retired row needs, and it is stored with your name and the time.

FilmPointRetireCreate.title: FilmPointRetireCreate
FilmPointRetireCreate.description:
T109 (D-109-4): take a point off the live list, keeping everything.

The point leaves the walk and stops feeding the dashboard for every
month. Its readings stay in History tagged `retired`, no car becomes
incomplete because of it, and a later upload that writes its label is
asked about in the row. RO17: restore puts it back; the last live point
of a list cannot be retired.

FilmPointSettingCreate.title: FilmPointSettingCreate
FilmPointSettingCreate.description:
T99 (D-99-4): change which points count, and their Hor / Ver.

Append-only: every point named here gets a **new** row. The row before it
is never changed or removed, and the latest row per point is what the
dashboard reads -- for every month, past ones included. A reason is
required because that is the thing a later reader needs.

label.title: Label
label.description: RO17 (D-RO17-1): the point's current label -- the word this plant uses for it. The code where it has no label row.

counted.title: Counted
counted.description: Latest film_point_setting.counted; true where none exists.

orientation.title: Orientation
orientation.description: Latest setting's Hor / Ver, else the catalogue's.

is_complete_stop.title: Is Complete Stop
is_complete_stop.description: T99 (D-99-8): a walk that ends exactly here is a complete vehicle (FTM RAPCAP 059RTFEND, DBL 064RAPILLAR).

is_extra.title: Is Extra
is_extra.description: T109 (D-109-3): this point is beyond the plant's standard list for the model -- FTM's 095RBXFLOOR and 096-098TGATEIN on the two DBL lists, and every point added since. A tag, not a grade: it changes no reading and refuses nothing.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the latest setting row says what it says.

changed_by.title: Changed By
changed_by.description: T115 (D-115-1): app_user.display_name of the person who wrote it; null for the seed, "-" for a user with no name.

changed_at.title: Changed At
changed_at.description: When it was written. Null where no setting row exists.

FilmPointSettingItem.title: FilmPointSettingItem
FilmPointSettingItem.description: One live point of a plant x model Film list, with its setting.

has_setting.title: Has Setting
has_setting.description: False where no film_point_setting row exists for this plant x model: the T99 rules are switched off there and the list behaves exactly as it did before (D-99-12).

items.title: Items
items.description: Every live point of the list, in walk order.

retired_items.title: Retired Items
retired_items.description: T109 (D-109-4). The points this list used to walk, in walk order, with when each went and why. Read-only, and never part of the live list: a retired point is not expected on a car, is not in the walk, and feeds no box. Its readings are still in History, tagged. Empty where nothing has been retired.

tail_labels.title: Tail Labels
tail_labels.description: RO17 (D-RO17-12). The known tail of this walk (FTWISH, BOOTH_1): labels that are never a fact and never a hold. Live and retired; a retired one is a record only.

FilmPointSettingOut.title: FilmPointSettingOut
FilmPointSettingOut.description: T99 (D-99-2, D-99-4): the remembered setting of one plant x model.

label.title: Label
label.description: RO17 (D-RO17-1): the point's current label -- the word this plant uses for it. The code where it has no label row.

orientation.title: Orientation
orientation.description: The Hor / Ver the catalogue row carries. For reading only.

is_extra.title: Is Extra
is_extra.description: T109 (D-109-3): it was beyond the plant's standard list.

retired_reason.title: Retired Reason
retired_reason.description: Why, as the person wrote it. This is the whole point of keeping the row: a reader of History's 'retired point' tag can find out what happened from here.

FilmRetiredPointItem.title: FilmRetiredPointItem
FilmRetiredPointItem.description: T109 (D-109-4): one point this plant's list used to walk.

target.title: Target
target.description: CLEAR only: the avg target (lo <= target <= hi).

operator_message.title: Operator Message
operator_message.description: The sentence the parse itself wrote. Show it as-is.

model_code.title: Model Code
model_code.description: The model the sheet is read as, when one is known.

confirmable.title: Confirmable
confirmable.description: kind=walk only: whether the uploader may confirm it. False means show the sentence and no button.

appended.title: Appended
appended.description: kind=walk + confirmable: the new names, in file order.

models.title: Models
models.description: kind=model: the two model codes the sheet names -- the Job Number's first, then the file name's. Empty otherwise.

job_no.title: Job No
job_no.description: kind=job (and kind=model): the Job Number as written.

FilmSheetQuestion.title: FilmSheetQuestion
FilmSheetQuestion.description:
T100 (D-100-1, D-100-5): the one question a held Film sheet asks.

Filled by the server from the same code that decided the hold, so the
screen never reads meaning out of a sentence. Null for a WaveScan tab and
for a Film tab with no sheet-wide hold.

One question per sheet, answered once, not per row:

* ``walk`` with ``confirmable`` -- the sheet wrote names past the end of
  the list. ``appended`` is those names with the H/V the list proposes.
  ``POST .../film-walk-confirm``.
* ``walk`` without ``confirmable`` -- the walk inserts, reorders,
  renumbers or repeats a name. ``operator_message`` says which, and there
  is **no button**: it needs an owner decision (D-99-14).
* ``model`` -- the file name and the Job Number name two different
  models. ``models`` is the two. ``POST .../film-model-answer``.
* ``job`` -- the Job Number is not this plant's shape. ``job_no`` is it,
  as written. ``POST .../film-job-answer``.

plant_code.title: Plant Code
plant_code.description: AAT, FTM, FVL or SAP. The rule applies to this plant only.

color_name.title: Color Name
color_name.description: NULL = plant-wide layer rule. Set = plant x colour rule; the colour must be offered at this plant (D-FS-08).

rules.title: Rules
rules.description: Latest row per (layer, colour-or-NULL, orient) at this plant. A reading uses its colour's rule, else the plant-wide one, else none.

weeks.title: Weeks
weeks.description: Weeks descending, weeks with no matching cars omitted. An empty list is an empty state, not a zero KPI.

active_data_source.title: Active Data Source
active_data_source.description: The view these facts were read through: not a duplicate, not superseded (01-DATA-MODEL.md section 10). Review rows, held labels (extra points, unmapped locations) and abandoned batches are never facts, so they are absent by construction.

FilmTailLabelCreate.title: FilmTailLabelCreate
FilmTailLabelCreate.description:
RO17 (D-RO17-12): Admin. A label this walk writes that is no point.

Rows with it are skipped on upload -- never a fact, never a hold. Refused
when it names a live point (its readings would vanish). A retired one is
put back.

FilmTailLabelItem.title: FilmTailLabelItem
FilmTailLabelItem.description: RO17 (D-RO17-12): one tail label of a plant x model Film walk.

FilmTailLabelRetireCreate.title: FilmTailLabelRetireCreate
FilmTailLabelRetireCreate.description: RO17 (D-RO17-12): Admin. Rows with this label are asked about again.

raw_location.title: Raw Location
raw_location.description: The Location exactly as the file wrote it.

rows.title: Rows
rows.description: How many rows of this tab carry the label. The question is answered once for all of them: a Cab sheet writing one retired name on four rows is one answer and then four loaded readings.

FilmUnknownLabel.title: FilmUnknownLabel
FilmUnknownLabel.description: T109 (D-109-6): one label this Film tab is asking about.

logical_vehicle_id.title: Logical Vehicle Id
logical_vehicle_id.description: filmthickness.logical_vehicle_id (T46, spec section 6): 64-hex SHA-256 of 'plant|measured_date|model|colour|identity', identity being 'vin:<VIN>', else 'job:<Job Number>', else 'blank'. load_id is NOT inside it: a Cab walk and a Box walk of one car are one vehicle.

serial_no.title: Serial No
serial_no.description: VIN when the file carried one.

date_is_month_only.title: Date Is Month Only
date_is_month_only.description: RO18 (B4): the sheet had no date. measured_date is the 1st of the month a person named; show '<Month YYYY> - day not recorded'. Such cars never pair.

job_nos.title: Job Nos
job_nos.description: Distinct Job Numbers across the vehicle's loads, sorted. Empty when none. Identity is the VIN when there is one, so two loads of one VIN may carry two job numbers.

identity_complete.title: Identity Complete
identity_complete.description: False when neither a VIN nor a Job Number identifies the car: the id then groups by plant, day, model and colour only. Nothing is generated to fill the gap.

load_ids.title: Load Ids
load_ids.description: Committed load_batch ids that contributed facts, ascending. Provenance, not identity.

source_files.title: Source Files
source_files.description: load_batch.source_file of those loads, in load_ids order.

mapped_point_count.title: Mapped Point Count
mapped_point_count.description: Gold points of this model with at least one active layer value, counted as distinct point_code across every load.

expected_point_count.title: Expected Point Count
expected_point_count.description: T54: the size of this plant's gold list for this model (ref_plant_film_point; 94 for P703 DBL Ranger / Raptor at FVL and FTM, 94 for FTM RAPCAP / Single CAP too, whose walks fill only the names they have). Null when the plant has none.

incomplete.title: Incomplete
incomplete.description: True when mapped_point_count differs from expected_point_count, or expected_point_count is null. A fact, not a grade.

box.title: Box
box.description: T103 (D-103-1): 'box' when this car has a reading after the lowest point its list may complete at (ref_plant_film_point is_complete_stop), 'no_box' when it has none. Null when that list names no stop. An FTM Single CAP car is always 'no_box': its only stop is its last point, so its box section is empty (D-103-2). A fact about the walk, not a grade.

identity_note.title: Identity Note
identity_note.description: T103 (D-103-6): the warning this car's loaded rows carry, as stored when they loaded (D-99-11: the Job Number's colour code and the file name's disagreeing). Null when they carry none. Read from stg_review_row.detail; nothing is re-parsed and no sentence is written here.

FilmVehicleOut.title: FilmVehicleOut
FilmVehicleOut.description: One car's film facts, across every committed file that measured it.

week.title: Week
week.description: T108: echo of the week band asked for, or null for the whole month. The band is the server's (`domain.history.measured_week`), so the cars of a week card are the cars that card counted.

active_data_source.title: Active Data Source
active_data_source.description: The view these facts were read through: not a duplicate, not superseded (01-DATA-MODEL.md section 10). Review rows, held labels (extra points, unmapped locations) and abandoned batches are never facts, so they are absent by construction.

FilmWalkConfirmCreate.title: FilmWalkConfirmCreate
FilmWalkConfirmCreate.description:
T99 (D-99-14): confirm the names appended after the known walk.

Every appended name must be answered and nothing else may be: a name
inside the known walk is a renumber, which no confirm can make safe.

point_code.title: Point Code
point_code.description: The point name exactly as the sheet wrote it. Identity is number and name (D-99-1), so the digits are part of it.

counted.title: Counted
counted.description: Whether this point feeds the dashboard's Hor / Ver.

orientation.title: Orientation
orientation.description: Horizontal or Vertical. Pre-filled by the rule (Hood, Roof, Box-floor are H; everything else V); a word the rule does not know has to be chosen.

FilmWalkPoint.title: FilmWalkPoint
FilmWalkPoint.description: One name this sheet appended to the walk, with what it is.

week.title: Week
week.description: Day bands of measured_date, the same rule as WaveScan History: 1 = days 1-7, 2 = 8-14, 3 = 15-21, 4 = 22-28, 5 = 29 to the end of that month (02-PIPELINE.md section 8.1).

raw_value.title: Raw Value
raw_value.description: The cell text as the file spelled it.

teachable_kind.title: Teachable Kind
teachable_kind.description: ALIAS_COLOR or ALIAS_MODEL when that kind is implemented for this reason; null when the row stays held (named-owner catalogue, leftover without its own ref_model, or a reserved kind).

candidates.title: Candidates
candidates.description: Existing catalogue codes for this field. Empty if none. **T89 (D-89-6)** for a panel question: the same list the guided match screen offers, in the same order -- mappable panels only, orientation-filtered, with the panels this batch has already used moved to `blocked_candidates`. Before T89 this was the plant's raw live panel list, half of which the approval path refuses.

blocked_candidates.title: Blocked Candidates
blocked_candidates.description: T89 (D-89-6). Panels this file has already used, for a panel question: shown last, disabled, each labelled with the spelling that took it. Empty for every other kind of question.

carried_over.description: T89 (D-89-9). An earlier decision about this exact spelling, so the row arrives pre-selected and marked as carried over instead of blank. Null when there is none; never auto-applied.

display_group.title: Display Group
display_group.description: Which question this is. T39 adds `plant` (the Plant column names another plant than the page) and `measure` (CF, or LW/SW, empty). T54 adds `film_point` (a FilmThickness location not on this plant's gold list, or an extra point) and `film_model` (the file or tab name does not settle one model this plant has a FilmThickness list for -- DBL / RB / RAP / SGL, or a leftover's own U704 / CX743 / V363 / J73 since T55). Neither is teachable here.

film_model.description: T61 (D-78-34). Present only when `reason` is `FILM_MODEL_UNRESOLVED`: the server-derived model choices and teachable tokens for this sheet. Null for every other reason.

model_code.title: Model Code
model_code.description: T41 / T88. The model this panel question is about. **T88 (D-88-1):** a spelling written on more than one model produces one group per model, each carrying its own model, its own row `count` and its own `candidates` -- they are independent questions, not one ambiguity. Send it as ALIAS_CHECKZONE payload.model_code. Null for a hold that is not about a panel, or whose Model cell resolved to nothing.

orientations.title: Orientations
orientations.description: T88 (D-88-2 / G-88-5). The Tolerance Group values the file wrote for this spelling on this model -- normally one, `Horizontal` or `Vertical`. It is a **hard filter on proposals** in the guided match screen and never a score. More than one entry is a file problem: the screen says so and applies no orientation filter and no exhaustion for that spelling.

HeldLabelGroup.title: HeldLabelGroup
HeldLabelGroup.description:
One distinct held spelling on a batch (finish-batch spec section 4).

Grouped from the persisted review projection, so a GET never opens Excel.
`teachable_kind` is set only when Engineer identity-alias is implemented
for that reason. Candidates are existing catalogue codes, never invented.

raw_zone_text.title: Raw Zone Text
raw_zone_text.description: The Checkzone cell as the file spells it.

raw_position.title: Raw Position
raw_position.description: The label's own leading number, 1-40, or null. Provenance only (S14): it is shown beside the name and never drives a proposal.

reasons.title: Reasons
reasons.description: Why it is held: UNKNOWN_CHECKZONE (on no list here) and/or ZONE_NOT_VALID_FOR_MODEL (a real panel another model owns). Both ask the same question on this screen.

candidates.title: Candidates
candidates.description: Live panels this spelling could be, best first. **T88:** the list is filtered by orientation first (a hard constraint, never a score) and then ranked by T86/T87's family, name and number. Empty is an answer, not a gap to fill with the nearest number.

orientations.title: Orientations
orientations.description: T88. The Tolerance Group values the file wrote for this spelling on this model. One is normal; more than one is a file problem and switches the orientation filter and exhaustion off for this spelling (G-88-5).

proposed_zone_code.title: Proposed Zone Code
proposed_zone_code.description: T88. The panel the solver would pair this spelling with, or null. **Never an answer** -- a person confirms every pair (D-88-3).

signal.title: Signal
signal.description: T88 (D-88-3). Which signal argued for `proposed_zone_code`: `name`, `number`, `exhaustion`, or `none` (no proposal, or a pair the owner already confirmed). Shown in the screen so the owner sees what argued for a pair; nothing branches on it.

signal_reason.title: Signal Reason
signal_reason.description: T88. The same thing in plain words, including -- for an exhaustion claim -- the counts it rests on (G-88-3).

orientation_conflict.title: Orientation Conflict
orientation_conflict.description: T88 (G-88-5). True when this spelling's own rows disagree about Tolerance Group. The orientation filter and exhaustion are both switched off for it, and the screen says so.

filtered_out.title: Filtered Out
filtered_out.description: T88 (G-88-5). Panels the orientation filter removed from the **proposals**. They stay choosable: a constraint narrows what is suggested and never what the owner may pick.

choosable.title: Choosable
choosable.description: T89 (D-89-6). **The** list this spelling may be answered with, suggestions first and then the rest in walk order: mappable panels only, orientation-filtered, with the panels this batch has already used taken out. The per-row picker in the held-label list is built from the same call, so the two pickers are the same list in the same order and no panel the approval path would refuse is ever offered.

blocked.title: Blocked
blocked.description: T89 (D-89-6). Panels of the right orientation this file has already used: shown last, disabled, each labelled with the spelling that took it.

carried_over.description: T89 (D-89-9). An earlier decision about this spelling, to arrive pre-selected and marked as carried over. Null when there is none. Never auto-applied.

walk.description: T90. This spelling's place in the structural reading of the whole walk: its colour, its reason, and what each rule says it is. Null when the walk has nothing to say about it. The same row appears in `walk.rows`, which covers every name the file writes rather than only the held ones.

HeldPanelOut.title: HeldPanelOut
HeldPanelOut.description: One distinct panel spelling the file wrote and this plant held.

vehicle_count.title: Vehicle Count
vehicle_count.description: Distinct vehicle sets, not distinct serials: two sheets that measured the same serial on the same day are two vehicles.

point_count.title: Point Count
point_count.description: Active measurement rows. Summing a month's cards gives the same number as GET /measurements page.total for the same plant, month, model and colour.

HistoryCardOut.title: HistoryCardOut
HistoryCardOut.description: One model + colour card inside a week (design F13).

plant_is_active.title: Plant Is Active
plant_is_active.description: False for a known plant this platform has not onboarded (FVL, D5). Its History is an empty set of months rather than an error.

default_month.title: Default Month
default_month.description: The latest month with at least one active row for this plant, YYYY-MM, or null when the plant has none.

months.title: Months
months.description: Months of measured_date that have active rows, newest first.

month.title: Month
month.description: Echo of the query, or null.

models.title: Models
models.description: Models present in the selected month, sorted. Empty when no month was given: there is nothing to cascade from.

colors.title: Colors
colors.description: Colours present in the selected month, narrowed to the selected model when one was given. Empty when no month was given.

active_data_source.title: Active Data Source
active_data_source.description: The view these numbers were read through. It applies the active-data predicate -- not a duplicate, not retired, batch committed -- in one place (01-DATA-MODEL.md section 10). Superseded facts and abandoned reviews are absent by construction.

HistoryFacetsOut.title: HistoryFacetsOut
HistoryFacetsOut.description:
The cascading pick lists for Month -> Model -> Colour (design F14).

They are API fields because the alternative is the client downloading
every active row to fold its own lists.

checkzone.title: Checkzone
checkzone.description: Stored zone_code. Identity for grading and grids. Since T58 a new load stores that plant x model's own gold name (FVL `11ROOF`, SAP `01RHS Hood Rr28`); AAT/FTM long-form may store `RRHOOD`. Earlier facts keep what they stored.

panel_label.title: Panel Label
panel_label.description: The panel to show people. T94 (D-94-4): this is the stored position -- the long name -- so a rough spelling is never displayed as a position. A reading the file called `01HOOD` and a person confirmed as RRHOOD reads `RRHOOD` here. Before T94 this was src_zone_text (T53, D-53-09); the file's own words are now carried beside it as src_zone_text instead, so nothing is lost. Equals checkzone by construction.

src_zone_text.title: Src Zone Text
src_zone_text.description: T94 (D-94-4): the panel exactly as the plant wrote it in the file (`01HOOD`, `01 RRHOOD`, `06LFFENDER`), for provenance -- show it beside the position, never as the position. Null for a fact stored without source text.

tolerance_group.title: Tolerance Group
tolerance_group.description: Horizontal or Vertical; a property of the zone.

date_is_month_only.title: Date Is Month Only
date_is_month_only.description: RO18 (B4): measured_date is the 1st of a named month; the day is not recorded.

corrects_measurement_id.title: Corrects Measurement Id
corrects_measurement_id.description: Set when this row is a correction of an earlier measurement.

retired.title: Retired
retired.description: T114: the point was retired on this plant's list. The reading stays here; it no longer feeds the dashboard.

counted.title: Counted
counted.description: T114: the point's latest ws_point_setting.counted (no row = counted). False: the reading stays here and leaves the dashboard.

IgnoredHeader.title: IgnoredHeader

RoughPanelOut.title: RoughPanelOut
RoughPanelOut.description:
T94 (D-94-1): one panel name of this tab that does not name a panel.

A label is **rough** when, with its leading number dropped, it names
more than one canonical panel of its `(plant, model)` -- `01HOOD` names
five hoods -- or when another label of the same sheet reduces to the
same name -- `06`/`07`/`08LFFENDER`. Otherwise it is specific and loads
without being asked about, and does not appear here.

This is what the highlighted row in the confirm table renders: the long
name we propose already chosen, the reason in words, and the whole list
to pick from if the proposal is wrong. Nothing is applied until a person
confirms it (D-94-6).

SupersedeCreate.title: SupersedeCreate
SupersedeCreate.description:
Retire a whole committed batch.

This is **not** a per-row supersession. The active-data predicate already
hides a batch's facts once its status leaves `COMMITTED`
(`01-DATA-MODEL.md` §5), so retiring the batch is one status change, not
one `measurement_supersession` row per measurement. Per-row supersession
is what a *correction* does, and it means something different: that one
reading was replaced by another.

WalkGroupCountOut.description: One panel family, counted in the file and in the canonical list.

fingerprint.title: Fingerprint
fingerprint.description: The ordered group sequence, `|`-joined. The stored form: this is what a confirmed set is remembered under (D-90-4, D-90-11).

fingerprint_display.title: Fingerprint Display
fingerprint_display.description: The same thing to read: "H H H H H F F F D D R P D ...".

group_counts.title: Group Counts
group_counts.description: File against canonical, per family. This is the multiset test.

multiset_matches.title: Multiset Matches
multiset_matches.description: True when every family appears as often as it does canonically.

walk_order_verified.title: Walk Order Verified
walk_order_verified.description: D-90-7. True when the leading numbers ascend within every vehicle and the panels first appear in walk order. **Checked, not assumed**: where it is false rule (a) is withheld entirely and every row is red, and the sheet is still never refused (D-90-13).

rule_group_ordinal_reason.title: Rule Group Ordinal Reason
rule_group_ordinal_reason.description: Why rule (a) does or does not apply, in plain words.

disagreements.title: Disagreements
disagreements.description: D-90-2. Names the two rules answer differently. When this is not empty **no** row of the set is yellow: a disagreement is information about the whole alignment, not noise on one line.

fingerprint_moved.title: Fingerprint Moved
fingerprint_moved.description: True when a set was confirmed before and this file does not walk it.

confirmed_before.title: Confirmed Before
confirmed_before.description: True when any walk has been confirmed for this plant x model.

confirmed_load_id.title: Confirmed Load Id
confirmed_load_id.description: The batch the remembered set was confirmed on. D-90-11: a confirmed **rough** mapping lives on the batch and nowhere else, because nothing on the resolution path can read a batch.

red_count.title: Red Count
red_count.description: D-90-14. Bulk accept confirms the yellow rows only and reports both numbers -- '28 accepted, 4 still need you'. A red is never swept along.

operator_message.title: Operator Message
operator_message.description: D-90-5. What one click would do, in the owner's words -- *same walk as September, confirmed 9 Oct, accept all 32* -- or why there is no such click yet. Never silence: even an unchanged walk is confirmed, once, by a person.

rows.title: Rows
rows.description: One per distinct name the file writes, in walk order.

WalkMatchOut.title: WalkMatchOut
WalkMatchOut.description:
T90: the whole structural reading of one `(plant, model)`'s walk.

**The walk is the identity; the label is only a label.** Three months of
real FTM files describe the same 32-point walk under three naming
schemes, so this block is about the *structure* the file writes and not
about its spellings: `fingerprint` is the ordered sequence of panel
**groups** (D-90-4), deliberately not the names, so a respelling does
not invalidate a confirmed walk while a reshuffle does.

Null on the parent when the sheet writes no panel name for this model,
or when the model has no canonical list to align against at all.

raw_zone_text.title: Raw Zone Text
raw_zone_text.description: The panel name as the file spells it.

panel_group.title: Panel Group
panel_group.description: HOOD / FENDER / DOOR / ROOF / PILLAR / BOX / TAILGATE, or null.

side.title: Side
side.description: `L`, `R` or null, read from the letters in front of the family word. `LCROOF` carries a side; `ROOF`, `HOOD` and `TGATE` carry none, and an absent side is never cross-checked against a present one (D-90-8).

specificity.title: Specificity
specificity.description: T90 (D-90-3). `rough` when this name's core is shared with another name of the same sheet -- then the **number** is doing the identifying and the name alone names no position. `specific` when it is not. A rough confirmation is recorded on the batch and is **never** written to `ref_plant_zone_map`.

binding.title: Binding
binding.description: T91 (D-91-3). How far confirming this pair may travel, said in the data: `alias` becomes a permanent `ref_plant_zone_map` row, `batch` is confirmed for this upload only and recorded on it (D-90-11). Two things make it `batch` -- a rough name (D-90-3), and a name another sheet of this plant confirmed as a **different** panel (D-91-2). The second holds even for a `specific` name: `13LFRDOOR` is a pillar in August and a door in September, so at FTM that spelling identifies no panel on its own and can never be learned forever again. Offering a `batch` row as a permanent alias is refused at the write boundary; this field is so the screen says it first.

binding_reason.title: Binding Reason
binding_reason.description: Why it is `batch`, in plain words, naming the file that confirmed it differently. Null when it is `alias`.

attention.title: Attention
attention.description: `yellow` (looks right, still confirm) or `red`. There is no green.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why it is that colour, in plain words.

rule.title: Rule
rule.description: `group_ordinal` (rule a), `walk_number` (rule b) or `none` (rule c: no structural rule applies, or the two disagree).

proposed_zone_code.title: Proposed Zone Code
proposed_zone_code.description: What the rules agree this name is, or null. Null when no rule applies **and** when the two rules disagree -- a disagreement proposes neither answer (D-90-2). Never applied without a click.

rule_walk_number_zone_code.title: Rule Walk Number Zone Code
rule_walk_number_zone_code.description: Rule (b)'s own answer, or null. Both are carried so a disagreement can be shown whole rather than summarised.

side_hint_checked.title: Side Hint Checked
side_hint_checked.description: True when the file's name and the proposed panel both carried a side and they were compared. False means there was nothing to compare -- `25TGATE`..`29TGATE` -- which is why that group is red the first time a walk is seen (D-90-12).

prefilled_zone_code.title: Prefilled Zone Code
prefilled_zone_code.description: The answer confirmed last under this same walk, to arrive pre-filled. Null when the walk has changed or nothing was confirmed before. Never an answer.

WalkRowOut.title: WalkRowOut
WalkRowOut.description:
T90: the structural verdict for one name the file writes.

**Two colours and no green** (D-90-6). `attention` is `yellow` ("looks
right, still confirm") only when a rule applied cleanly, any side hint
agreed, and the answer is what was confirmed last under this same walk.
Everything else is `red`, and `reason` says which of those it was in
plain words -- the colour on its own is a demand without a case.

measured_date.title: Measured Date
measured_date.description: Date the reading was measured, from its own row.

checkzone.title: Checkzone
checkzone.description: The reading's own canonical checkzone (point / zone label).

cf.title: Cf
cf.description: The reading's own CF, exact and unrounded.

WavescanBelowMinimumReading.title: WavescanBelowMinimumReading
WavescanBelowMinimumReading.description:
One reading of a box below that box's own Minimum (T73 D-73-01).

Listed, never graded on its own: the box status is still the mean's.

readings.title: Readings
readings.description: Counted readings in the month and filters.

below_minimum.title: Below Minimum
below_minimum.description: Readings listed below their box's Minimum.

readings.title: Readings
readings.description: Counted readings in the month and filters.

below_minimum.title: Below Minimum
below_minimum.description: Readings listed below their box's Minimum.

models.title: Models
models.description: Selected model_code values. Empty means every measured model.

colors.title: Colors
colors.description: Selected colour names. Empty means every offered colour.

active_data_source.title: Active Data Source
active_data_source.description: The view these numbers were read through: v_wavescan_active narrowed to readings whose point is live and counted (T114). Quartiles, the mean and status cover every matching counted row — there is no point cap.

profiles.title: Profiles
profiles.description: The template profiles that parsed this workbook's sheets. Where a sheet has a projection, the fingerprint shown is the one that actually parsed it, not the frozen load_batch.template_fingerprint recorded at upload.

acknowledgements.title: Acknowledgements
acknowledgements.description: Every acknowledgement ever written for these sheets, oldest first, including ones a replay has invalidated -- compare review_revision with the sheet's current one.

events.title: Events
events.description: Oldest first, by audit_event.id. Append-only: no role holds UPDATE or DELETE on audit_event.

measurements_inserted.title: Measurements Inserted
measurements_inserted.description: Fact rows written. For FilmThickness that is one per layer, so it can be up to four times readings_added.

readings_added.title: Readings Added
readings_added.description: T54: readings the uploader added -- WaveScan points, or FilmThickness points (not layers). The toast counts these.

rows_held.title: Rows Held
rows_held.description: T53: rows of this workbook still held out after this click.

rows_already_in_history.title: Rows Already In History
rows_already_in_history.description: T53: rows that were already in History and were not added again.

months.title: Months
months.description: T53: months the added readings belong to, YYYY-MM, oldest first.

operator_message.title: Operator Message
operator_message.description: T53: the toast, e.g. "40 readings added to September 2026, 2 held out, 31 already in History." ASCII only.

file_hash.title: File Hash
file_hash.description: SHA-256 of the uploaded bytes. The identity.

source_file.title: Source File
source_file.description: The filename as uploaded. A label: a renamed file with the same bytes is the same workbook, and identity is the hash.

operational_summary.title: Operational Summary
operational_summary.description: Where this file is in the workflow. NOT a grade and not a pass rate: it is derived from its sheets' load_batch.status values only (docs/02-PIPELINE.md).

measured_date_min.title: Measured Date Min
measured_date_min.description: Earliest cleaned measurement date in this workbook, from the review projection for sheets in review and from wavescan for committed ones. Null while the worker is still parsing -- a week is never inferred from the upload time or the filename.

uploaded_at.title: Uploaded At
uploaded_at.description: Workbook upload time, or earliest legacy load_batch.started_at.

counts.description: Sum of this workbook's data batch counts, excluding skipped side sheets.

skipped_sheets.title: Skipped Sheets
skipped_sheets.description: Out-of-scope sheets kept under this file, excluded from data batch counts.

superseded.title: Superseded
superseded.description: True exactly when operational_summary is SUPERSEDED: no live sheet, and at least one SUPERSEDED. The rows stay readable.

abandoned.title: Abandoned
abandoned.description: True exactly when operational_summary is ABANDONED: every sheet was removed from review before producing a measurement. Bytes, staging, projection and history are retained (T21).

vehicle_set_count.title: Vehicle Set Count
vehicle_set_count.description: Vehicle sets across this workbook's sheets, grouped by the server exactly as the vehicles read groups them, including identity-incomplete groups. 0 while nothing has been parsed or committed yet.

measured_dates_span_months.title: Measured Dates Span Months
measured_dates_span_months.description: True when measured_date_min and measured_date_max fall in different calendar months. False when either is null.

WorkbookOut.title: WorkbookOut
WorkbookOut.description: One workbook: one file_hash at one plant, with its sheets as children.

plant_is_active.title: Plant Is Active
plant_is_active.description: False for a known plant this platform has not onboarded (FVL, D5). Its workbook list is an empty page rather than an error: the plant is shown with its reason, not hidden.

inbox.title: Inbox
inbox.description: The inbox this page was selected by (the query value).

uploaded_month.title: Uploaded Month
uploaded_month.description: The UTC month (YYYY-MM) current_month and needs_attention were decided against: the query value, or the current UTC month when none was sent. Null for inbox=all, which ignores it.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why this workbook should not exist in the database.
examples: Wrong layout loaded; will re-upload and map again.

WorkbookPurgeCreate.title: WorkbookPurgeCreate
WorkbookPurgeCreate.description: `{ reason }` and nothing else. The reason is stored on the audit row.

load_ids.title: Load Ids
load_ids.description: Every load_batch of this hash that was deleted.

note.title: Note
note.default: This workbook's batches, staging, review rows, rejects, jobs and wavescan rows were deleted. Published template profiles, aliases and standards are untouched. Uploading the same bytes again is a new batch.

canonical.title: Canonical
canonical.description: What commit would insert, or did insert, for this row.

raw.title: Raw
raw.description: What the file said: recognised values and unmapped extras. Null only when projection_missing is true.

normalized_fields.title: Normalized Fields
normalized_fields.description: Fields filled or mapped for this row rather than read from it. Today: plant, filled from the upload's expected_plant.

measurement_id.title: Measurement Id
measurement_id.description: The wavescan row this source row produced, once committed. Present for a superseded batch too: this is the file's own drill-down, not the active measurement list.

projection_missing.title: Projection Missing
projection_missing.description: True for a sheet committed before the review projection existed (T18). Its facts are shown with raw null; the workbook is never re-parsed to fill them in.

committable.title: Committable
committable.description: True only when committing this sheet right now would succeed. The same value GET /api/v1/batches/{load_id} publishes.

commit_blockers.title: Commit Blockers
commit_blockers.description: Stable tokens naming why this sheet cannot be committed: NOT_PENDING_REVIEW, UNBALANCED, UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE, UNVERIFIED_PROFILE, NO_REVIEW_PROJECTION, VEHICLE_IDENTITY_MISSING, WARNINGS_UNACKNOWLEDGED.

required_acknowledgements.title: Required Acknowledgements
required_acknowledgements.description: Warning categories this sheet must have acknowledged before it can be committed, because rows the plant sent are not becoming measurements.

acknowledged.title: Acknowledged
acknowledged.description: Categories already acknowledged for this sheet's CURRENT review_revision. A replay moves the revision, so an earlier acknowledgement stops appearing here while staying in the history.

WorkbookSheetOut.title: WorkbookSheetOut
WorkbookSheetOut.description: One sheet of a workbook: a `load_batch` plus its readiness.

plant_question.description: Set when the Plant column names something else. Answer it first.

missing_optional.title: Missing Optional
missing_optional.description: T42: optional fields at least one WaveScan tab has no column for, e.g. ["doi"]. Rows still load with those values empty.

missing_optional_message.title: Missing Optional Message
missing_optional_message.description: Plain sentence for missing_optional, e.g. "This file has no DOI column. Rows can still load with DOI empty." Null when nothing optional is missing.

rows_already_in_history.title: Rows Already In History
rows_already_in_history.description: T53: rows already in History across the workbook.

rows_need_confirmation.title: Rows Need Confirmation
rows_need_confirmation.description: T94: rows across the workbook whose panel name must be confirmed before they can load.

summary_message.title: Summary Message
summary_message.description: T53: the workbook in one plain sentence, e.g. "40 readings ready to add, 2 held out, 31 already in History." Uses only the words ready, held out and already in History.

checklist.title: Checklist
checklist.description: Short plain sentences, in the order to read them.

panel_label.title: Panel Label
panel_label.description: The panel exactly as the file wrote it (e.g. 01HOOD). This is the plant's own checkpoint name; show it as-is. T54: on a FilmThickness tab it is the Location cell (e.g. 021LAPILLAR).

checkzone.title: Checkzone
checkzone.description: The catalogue identity it resolved to. WaveScan: the zone_code -- since T58 that plant x model's own gold name (FVL `11ROOF`, SAP `01RHS Hood Rr28`) or the AAT/FTM long-form code (`RRHOOD`). T54 FilmThickness: the plant's gold point_code (FTM's own 94 names, never another plant's). Null when the row is held.

model_text.title: Model Text
model_text.description: Model as the file wrote it. Null on a FilmThickness tab: its model comes from the file name (DBL / RB / RAP / SGL).

color_text.title: Color Text
color_text.description: Colour as the file wrote it.

date_text.title: Date Text
date_text.description: Date as the file wrote it.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.description: ready: added when the uploader approves. held_out: not added; operator_message says why. already_in_history: this reading is already in History and is never written twice. needs_confirmation (T94, D-94-2): this row's panel name does not say which panel it is, so it is never ready -- not even when the catalogue holds a panel spelled exactly like it. Confirm the panel in this row (see rough_panels and POST .../panel-confirm) and the row becomes ready under the panel's long name.

operator_message.title: Operator Message
operator_message.description: One plain sentence for this row.

counted.title: Counted
counted.description: T100 (D-100-2). FilmThickness only: whether the latest setting says this row's point counts towards the dashboard's Hor / Ver. Show it as a **read-only** tick -- changing a known point happens on the Standard tab's Points panel, with a reason, because it rewrites past months. Null on a WaveScan tab, on a plant x model with no setting, and on a row that names no point.

film_tail.title: Film Tail
film_tail.description: T100 (D-100-4). True for a row the plant's walk is known to end with -- FTM 001FTWISH-006FTWISH and BOOTH_1. Show it as **Not stored**, muted, with no tick: it is never a fact, never a hold, and never a reason anything needs attention.

film_extra.title: Film Extra
film_extra.description: T109 (D-109-3). FilmThickness only: whether this row's point is beyond the plant's standard list for the model. Show it as a tag beside the point. Null on a WaveScan tab, on a plant x model with no setting, and on a row that resolved to no point.

WorksheetRowOut.title: WorksheetRowOut
WorksheetRowOut.description:
T53: one row of the uploaded workbook, as the confirm table shows it.

Read from the stored review projection (no workbook is opened). The
file's own words sit beside the catalogue name they resolved to, so the
uploader sees what they wrote. There is no CF or thickness field to edit
here, on purpose (ADR 0005).

state.title: State
state.description: ready: Yes loads it now. loaded: its good rows are measurements. needs_answer: a question below must be answered first. blocked: waiting on an Admin (template not proved, or unknown layout). processing: still being read. not_wavescan: an extra tab (cover, Methods, Color Data, pictures): "Extra tab kept. Not loaded." Not a broken template.

rows_held.title: Rows Held
rows_held.description: Rows that will not load until answered or fixed.

rows_already_in_history.title: Rows Already In History
rows_already_in_history.description: T53: rows whose reading is already in History (an earlier file, or this tab after it loaded). Never written twice.

rows_need_confirmation.title: Rows Need Confirmation
rows_need_confirmation.description: T94 (D-94-2): rows whose panel name does not say which panel it is. They are never ready. Confirm the panel in the row.

rows.title: Rows
rows.description: T53: every data row of this tab in file order, for the confirm table. Empty for an extra tab or a tab that could not be read.

extra_columns.title: Extra Columns
extra_columns.description: Columns we do not use. Ignore them to continue.

missing_optional.title: Missing Optional
missing_optional.description: T42: optional fields this tab has no column for (doi, serial_no, paintline, du, wa-we, b). A notice, not a refusal: rows load with those values empty.

hole_rows.title: Hole Rows
hole_rows.description: Source rows with CF but no LW/SW. They load only after the Engineer approves them (POST .../hole-approval).

plant_texts.title: Plant Texts
plant_texts.description: Plant cells on this sheet that do not name the page plant.

panel_rename.title: Panel Rename
panel_rename.description: T89 Part 5 (D-88-7). One entry per model of this tab whose panel set looks like a renaming of the whole walk. Empty is the normal answer.

rough_panels.title: Rough Panels
rough_panels.description: T94 (D-94-1, D-94-3). One entry per panel name of this tab that does not say which panel it is, with the long name we propose already chosen. The confirm table renders each of these IN the row that carries the name, highlighted, with one click to accept. Empty is the normal answer for a file whose names name their panels.

film_question.description: T100 (D-100-1, D-100-5). The one question this Film tab asks about itself -- its walk, which of two models it is, or its Job Number -- filled by the server from the code that decided the hold. Null for a WaveScan tab and for a Film tab with no sheet-wide hold. The screen renders it; it classifies nothing.

date_question.description: RO18 (B3 / B4). Which month (a sheet with no date anywhere, either domain) or which date (a Film sheet and its file name disagree by more than 3 days). Null when the tab asks neither.

film_box.title: Film Box
film_box.description: T103 (D-103-1): 'box' / 'no_box' for a Film tab whose walk was read -- the same rule and the same words GET .../filmthickness/vehicles answers with, so the review and History cannot disagree. Null for a WaveScan tab, a tab still held, and a plant x model whose list names no complete stop.

film_unknown_labels.title: Film Unknown Labels
film_unknown_labels.description: T109 (D-109-6). One entry per label on this Film tab that the plant's live list for the model does not hold -- a point that was retired, a spelling this plant has started writing. Each is asked about in its own row and answered once for every row that carries it; every other reading on the tab still loads. Empty for a WaveScan tab and for a Film tab whose labels all resolved.

film_point_choices.title: Film Point Choices
film_point_choices.description: T109 (D-109-6). The live points an answer may name: this plant's list for the tab's model, in walk order, with each point's Hor / Ver and extra tag. The same list Point Check shows. Sent only while the tab has a label to ask about, so a client never has to filter it, and never invents a candidate.

WsCompletenessImpactOut.title: WsCompletenessImpactOut
WsCompletenessImpactOut.description:
RO17 (D-RO17-7): what counting a new point in completeness would do.

Measured by doing the add inside a savepoint that is always rolled back.

zone_code.title: Zone Code
zone_code.description: An existing ref_checkzone code (zone_choices), or a new one. A new code equal to an existing one ignoring case and spaces is refused 409 -- pick the existing one.

counted_in_completeness.title: Counted In Completeness
counted_in_completeness.description: RO17 (D-RO17-7). False (default): the point is tagged extra and car completeness ignores it, as before. True (Admin only, else 403): it counts in completeness, and the result says how many stored cars became incomplete (ask completeness-impact first).

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why this point exists. Stored with your name and the time.

WsPointAddCreate.title: WsPointAddCreate
WsPointAddCreate.description:
D-114-6: add a point at the end of this plant's walk for the model.

Pick an existing zone code or type a new one. A new code is kept exactly
as typed after trimming its ends; its Hor / Ver is read off the name. The
point is tagged extra.

incomplete_cars.title: Incomplete Cars
incomplete_cars.description: RO17 (D-RO17-7): stored cars of this plant x model that became INCOMPLETE because the added point counts in completeness. Null unless counted_in_completeness was true.

WsPointChangeResult.title: WsPointChangeResult
WsPointChangeResult.description: What an add, a retire or a restore did, in the list's own terms.

zone_code.title: Zone Code
zone_code.description: The point's identity, the plant's own panel text.

label.title: Label
label.description: RO17 (D-RO17-1): the point's current label, the word its plant uses (newest label row; the code where none). Show it first, the code second.

tolerance_group.title: Tolerance Group
tolerance_group.description: Horizontal or Vertical, fixed by the name (ck_zone_rule: Hood, Roof or Floor in it is Horizontal). Shown, never edited.

counted.title: Counted
counted.description: Latest ws_point_setting.counted; true where none exists. False takes its readings off the dashboard for every month; History and Comparison keep them, tagged.

is_extra.title: Is Extra
is_extra.description: T114 (D-114-5): beyond the plant's standard list. Every point added on Point Check. A tag, not a grade.

note.title: Note
note.description: Where the row came from (T58 lock, a Point Check add).

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the latest setting row says what it says.

changed_by.title: Changed By
changed_by.description: T115 (D-115-1): app_user.display_name of who wrote it; null where no setting row exists, "-" for a user with no name.

changed_at.title: Changed At
changed_at.description: When. Null where no setting row exists.

WsPointItem.title: WsPointItem
WsPointItem.description: One live point of a plant x model Wave Scan list.

items.title: Items
items.description: Every live point, in walk order.

retired_items.title: Retired Items
retired_items.description: Every retired row of this list, in walk order, with when and why. Never part of the live list: not a panel-match target, never pre-filled, off the dashboard. Its readings stay in History, tagged.

zone_choices.title: Zone Choices
zone_choices.description: Every ref_checkzone code that is not already on this list, live or retired: what Add may pick. A code typed that is not here is a new code.

horizontal_words.title: Horizontal Words
horizontal_words.description: The words that make a name Horizontal (ck_zone_rule), so a screen can show a new code's Hor / Ver before it is sent. The server applies the same rule and the database enforces it.

WsPointListOut.title: WsPointListOut
WsPointListOut.description: D-114-1: what Point Check's Wave Scan section shows for one model.

point_count.title: Point Count
point_count.description: Live points on this plant's list.

counted_count.title: Counted Count
counted_count.description: Live points the dashboard counts (latest setting, no row = counted).

extra_count.title: Extra Count
extra_count.description: Live points tagged extra (D-114-5): beyond the standard list.

WsPointModelOut.title: WsPointModelOut
WsPointModelOut.description: One Wave Scan model this plant has a live point list for.

items.title: Items
items.description: Models with a live Wave Scan list at this plant, by model_code.

offered_without_list.title: Offered Without List
offered_without_list.description: RO17 (D-RO17-10): Wave Scan models this plant offers that have no live list yet. Their list reads as empty, and an Engineer may add its first point.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why it is back. Stored with your name and the time.

WsPointRestoreCreate.title: WsPointRestoreCreate
WsPointRestoreCreate.description: RO17 (D-RO17-9): bring a retired point back at its own number.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why this point is gone. Stored with your name and the time.

WsPointRetireCreate.title: WsPointRetireCreate
WsPointRetireCreate.description: D-114-4: take a point off the live list, keeping everything.

WsPointSettingCreate.title: WsPointSettingCreate
WsPointSettingCreate.description: D-114-2: change which points count. Append-only; latest row wins.

label.title: Label
label.description: RO17 (D-RO17-1): the point's current label, the word its plant uses (newest label row; the code where none). Show it first, the code second.

retired_reason.title: Retired Reason
retired_reason.description: Why, as the person or task wrote it.

WsRetiredPointItem.title: WsRetiredPointItem
WsRetiredPointItem.description: One point this plant's list used to walk.

WsZoneChoice.title: WsZoneChoice
WsZoneChoice.description: One existing zone code Add may pick, with the Hor / Ver it carries.
